Trading Economics data summary, read 08:47 BST (data only)

US 10 Year Treasury Note Yield - Summary The yield on the US 10-year Treasury note fell to around 5.11% on Thursday, hitting a three-week low and marking a sharp reversal after reaching as high as 5.33% in the previous session following the release of strong inflation data. The decline came as a deepening selloff in equity markets, led by technology and artificial intelligence stocks, drove investors toward safe-haven government bonds. Data released Wednesday showed that annual headline inflation accelerated to 3.7% in September, exceeding forecasts of 3.6%, while core inflation edged up to 2.6%, above expectations of 2.5%. Chicago Fed's Austan Goolsbee described the figures as “discouraging” and warned that the rapid expansion of AI-related infrastructure could also be overheating the economy. However, some policymakers continued to advocate a cautious approach toward further rate increases, with markets currently pricing in roughly a 73% probability that the Federal Reserve will leave interest rates unchanged this month. US 10 Year Treasury Note Yield - Stats The yield on US 10 Year Note Bond Yield eased to 5.10% on October 15, 2026, marking a 0.09 percentage points decrease from the previous session. Over the past month, the yield has edged up by 0.08 points and is 1.13 points higher than a year ago, according to over-the-counter interbank yield quotes for this government bond maturity. Historically, the US 10 Year Treasury Note Yield reached an all time high of 15.82 in September of 1981.
